note: Listen thread narration (threads-scripts §10). Wilson's words in listen-5 need L&GH rights clearance before this ships.

lines.listen-1: Close your eyes, or don't. This is Euclid Avenue at E. 40th, October 1888.
lines.listen-2: The street was paved in Medina sandstone blocks in 1873. People who lived here remembered the sound of hooves on it, and carriages going by at night.
lines.listen-3: Listen east. The horsecars came up from Prospect and turned back onto Euclid right about here. West of this corner, no streetcars were allowed.
lines.listen-4: That church tower has bells. What you're hearing is them not ringing. They stayed silent while the old man across the street was alive.
lines.listen-5: On the south side, at 3730, the Germania Orchestra played for nearly six hundred guests. A florist who danced to it remembered a young man crossing the floor: "This is our waltz."
lines.listen-6: Sunday at St. Paul's: prancing horses, liveried coachmen, the girls from the Mittleberger School. On Easter, latecomers were turned away at the door.
lines.listen-7: Behind the Brush house, a wheel fifty-six feet across turned all day. Nobody wrote down what it sounded like. So we've left it silent.
lines.listen-9: Wilson's old radio station made rain by pouring sand through a tea strainer. Most of what you just heard is our best guess. The silence wasn't.
